rationale: A wins because it does the harder editor's work: it turns the launch into four real desks and treats the lawsuit as a live trust problem instead of pretending it is background noise. A's "Can a payroll vendor's AI tell you to reclassify a worker — and who's liable when it's wrong?" is a real legal-trade story with proof demands an editor would respect. B's best line, "with no accuracy numbers," is sharp, but "Deel is giving away the compliance layer it used to sell" invents a business-model fact the update never gave it, and refusing the litigation frame throws away the obvious skeptical read.
gaps_in_A: "turning that into a real-time classification risk engine" gets a little ahead of the facts; the update says the tool flags risks as a company hires, not that Deel has disclosed a real-time engine or how it uses its payroll data.

"Deel ships a free compliance AI" and "pressures rivals who'd charge" lean on pricing inference. The update says included for existing customers; it does not prove free forever, no renewal impact, or competitor pricing pressure.
"category-creation" is close to overclaiming. One product launch with no adoption, accuracy, or competitor evidence is a category question, not a category proof.
It should have made undisclosed accuracy/audit data its own headline-level angle, not just a proof hole inside other angles.
gaps_in_B: "Deel is giving away the compliance layer it used to sell" is the worst miss. The update does not say Deel used to sell this layer separately or is giving away something previously paid.
"The prevailing belief in the category is that AI can now absorb compliance work" is unsupported atmospheric filler. If you cannot source the belief, do not build the angle on it.

"A $12B company under litigation bets on AI" as `off-beat` is an overcorrection. The active corporate-espionage lawsuit is exactly the kind of trust/competition context a skeptical category reporter will use.

"Next step: `newsjack-detector`" is the wrong first move for this brief. The launch is already the peg; the urgent next work is accuracy data, liability terms, court-record fact-checking, and journalist-fit.
